docs.text: Keep Original and Revert Two controls decide what happens to your original mesh: the Keep Original checkbox and the Revert button. Keep Original Checkbox — default on On: after the crush, the original is hidden (eye icon off). It stays in the scene, so you can compare, or come back to it later. Off: the original is deleted . Only the crushed copy remains. The checkbox is in Advanced → Result . It is greyed out while LODs is on, because LODs always keep the original. Warning With Keep Original off, there is nothing to go back to. Revert needs the original. The panel shows a red warning under the main button when it is off: "Original will be deleted" for Decimate, "Keep Original is off: Revert won't work" for Remesh. Right after the crush, Blender's Undo (Ctrl+Z) can still take it back. Revert Button — the small icon next to Crush Revert deletes the selected crushed object and brings back its original: the original is un-hidden and selected. Works on crushed copies and on LOD objects. Select the crushed object first, not the hidden original. You can select several crushed objects and revert them together. Greyed out when none of the selected objects has an original to go back to, and while a crush is running. Only available for crushes made with Keep Original on (or with LODs). Remesh keeps its source in the scene (unlinked from the rig); with Keep Original on, Revert brings it back. When it is done, Blender's status bar says how many objects were reverted. Where the link is kept Each crushed object remembers its original, and this is saved in the .blend file. Revert still works after you save and reopen. If you delete the original yourself, the link is cleared and Revert is greyed out for that object.

docs.text: Source Types Step 1 of the panel asks what kind of model you have. The right method for that kind is used, and each kind starts at a sensible amount. There used to be a Mode menu (Auto, Scan, Sculpt, Hard Surface, Custom). It was removed in 2.9.3: it only ticked checkboxes, sometimes behind your back. The model is looked at and the method picked for you. unchanged Scan 3D scans and photogrammetry: noise, cracks, holes. 95% removed AI AI-generated models (Meshy, Tripo and others): split seams, baked texture atlas. 90% removed CAD CAD parts (STEP exports): crisp corners, long thin triangles, exact holes. 70% removed Hard Surface Subdivided high-poly hard surface: rounded bevels instead of crisp corners. 75% removed Organic Characters, creatures and sculpts: smooth, no hard edges. 90% removed Cloth Garments made of sewn panels. 85% removed You can change the amount afterwards. docs.text: Target Modes The Percent , Count and Budget buttons under 2 Output choose how you ask for an amount. They work for Decimate (triangles) and for Remesh (quads, see the end of this page). Triangle counts are measured on the evaluated mesh. That is the mesh you see in the viewport, with all modifiers applied. Percent Removes a share of the triangles. Set Reduction from 1% to 99%. The default is 50%. Reduction Typical use 20–40% Light clean-up 50–70% Background props, secondary assets 80–95% Distant objects, real-time assets Each selected object is reduced by the same percentage. A 100,000-triangle object and a 10,000-triangle object, both at 80%, end up with 20,000 and 2,000 triangles. Picking a Source sets a starting value (for example 95% for a scan, 70% for CAD). The preset menu (Light, Medium, Heavy, Extreme) and saved presets were removed: Percent is just the slider. Count Crushes each selected object to Target Triangles (default 5000). If an object already has fewer triangles than the target, its copy keeps the original's triangle count. If that is true for every selected object, the report says the copies were left unchanged. Use this when every object needs the same triangle count, for example a set of props that all share one budget per object. Budget Sets one triangle total for the whole selection ( Total Triangles , default 100,000). Count mode gives every object the same count. Percent mode gives every object the same share. Budget does neither. It removes detail where it costs the least, across all selected objects together. Big or detailed objects keep more triangles. Simple objects are cut harder. Objects never merge into each other. Each one comes back as its own crushed copy. If the budget is so low that an object would get no triangles at all, that object is skipped and left as it is. The report names it. Note Budget works on the selection as a whole. If you select only one object, the budget applies to that object alone. What happens to the result In every mode: The crushed copy goes into a Crushed collection at the scene root. The collection is created on the first crush. The copy has the same world transform as the original and the name <original name>_crushed . The copy keeps smooth shading if the original had any smooth faces. The report in Blender's status bar shows the triangle count before and after. Check the after number. Some settings stop a crush above the target. See Limits . LODs override the target mode. See LODs . With Remesh Remesh uses the same three buttons. The amount is turned into quads: the triangles the amount would keep, divided by two. The panel's readout shows tris → quads so you can see the number before you click. Remesh lands close to that count. See Remesh (Quads) .

docs.text: Quick Start The Polygon Crusher Panel Once the add-on is installed, open the N-panel → Polygon Crusher 9000 tab in the 3D Viewport. The panel goes top to bottom in four steps: Source — what kind of model this is. Output — Decimate (fewer triangles) or Remesh (clean quads), and how much you want left. Keep — Shading , Textures and, for hard-surface and CAD parts, Sharps . Crush — Symmetry , the Crush button (with Revert beside it) and Import and Crush... . Under these, a collapsed Advanced section holds everything else. The Settings Reference describes every control. Basic Workflow Select one or more mesh objects in the 3D Viewport. Under 1 Source , pick what the model is. Leave it on Auto if you are not sure: after the run the panel says what it took the model for ("Last run treated it as: ..."). See Source Types . Under 2 Output , pick Decimate or Remesh , then Percent , Count or Budget and set the value. Picking a source also sets a sensible starting amount (scans start at 95% removed, CAD parts at 70%). Under 3 Keep , leave Shading on. Switch on Textures if the model has a texture you want to keep. Click Crush . The add-on will: Evaluate each selected object's full modifier stack and work on the resulting mesh. Place the result in a Crushed collection at the scene root. Hide the original (or delete it, depending on Keep Original ). The result lands at the source's exact world transform and is named <original name>_crushed . The status bar shows a report with the triangle count before and after. Check it. Some options can stop a crush above the target. See Limits . While it works, the Crush button becomes a Cancel button and a progress bar. Click Cancel (or press ESC ) to stop. Choosing a Target Mode Use it when Percent You want to remove a share of the triangles from every object. Count Every object needs the same triangle count. Budget The whole selection has one triangle budget. Detail goes where it costs least. Under the target control, the panel shows a live readout ( before → after triangles , or tris → quads in Remesh), so you can see what the setting means before you click Crush. See Target Modes . Tips For 3D Scans and Photogrammetry Pick Scan under Source. It switches on the scan repairs by itself: cracks and small holes are closed and spikes are removed. Switch on Textures to keep the photo texture, or tick Bake to Textures in Advanced to put the detail into maps. See Clean Mesh and Scan Repair and Bake Maps and Auto UVs . To get clean quads instead of triangles, pick Remesh . For AI-Generated Models (Meshy, Tripo and others) Pick AI . Seams that split the model are welded and holes are closed. For CAD Parts Pick CAD . Corners stay crisp, round holes stay round and flat faces stay flat. Sharps is on by default. With Remesh you get a clean grid with quad loops along the hard edges. See Hard Surface and Sharps . For Subdivided High-Poly Hard Surface Pick Hard Surface . Rounded bevels keep their rows and flat areas become big clean triangles. For Characters, Creatures and Sculpts Pick Organic . Pick Remesh to get quads, and use Quad Density to give the face more of them. For Clothing Pick Cloth . Folds bend freely and sewn garments are remeshed as one piece. Keeping Detail in One Area Decimate: in Advanced, tick Protect and paint the area or select faces in Edit Mode. See Protect Areas . Remesh: use Quad Density instead. Making LODs Tick LODs in Advanced and click Crush LODs . See LODs . Working with Modifiers Polygon Crusher reads the evaluated mesh, which is whatever the viewport shows, including booleans, subdivision, and any other modifier on the stack. The original object and its modifiers are left untouched. The result is a fresh static mesh with no modifiers. Processing Multiple Objects Select all the objects you want to crush before clicking Crush . They run at the same time, up to one job per CPU core. Going Back Select the result and click the Revert button next to Crush. It deletes the result and brings back the original. This needs Keep Original to be on. See Keep Original and Revert . After Crushing After a Decimate, Last Crush at the bottom of Advanced shows the triangle counts, total time and passes for the active crushed object. Click Details for the time of each phase. After a Remesh, a status box under the Keep section says what the run did (the real quad count and any notes).

docs.title: Choosing a Target

docs.text: Pick Scan under Source. It switches on the scan repairs by itself: cracks and small holes are closed and spikes are removed. Switch on Textures to keep the photo texture, or tick Bake to Textures in Advanced to put the detail into maps. See Clean Mesh and Scan Repair and Bake Maps and Auto UVs . To get clean quads instead of triangles, pick Remesh .
docs.title: For 3D Scans and Photogrammetry

docs.text: Pick AI . Seams that split the model are welded and holes are closed.
docs.title: For AI-Generated Models (Meshy, Tripo and others)

docs.text: Pick CAD . Corners stay crisp, round holes stay round and flat faces stay flat. Sharps is on by default. With Remesh you get a clean grid with quad loops along the hard edges. See Hard Surface and Sharps .
docs.title: For CAD Parts

docs.text: Pick Hard Surface . Rounded bevels keep their rows and flat areas become big clean triangles.
docs.title: For Subdivided High-Poly Hard Surface

docs.text: Pick Organic . Pick Remesh to get quads, and use Quad Density to give the face more of them.
docs.title: For Characters, Creatures and Sculpts

docs.text: Pick Cloth . Folds bend freely and sewn garments are remeshed as one piece.
docs.title: For Clothing

docs.text: Decimate: in Advanced, tick Protect and paint the area or select faces in Edit Mode. See Protect Areas . Remesh: use Quad Density instead.
docs.title: Keeping Detail in One Area

docs.text: Tick LODs in Advanced and click Crush LODs . See LODs .
docs.title: Making LODs

docs.text: Polygon Crusher reads the evaluated mesh, which is whatever the viewport shows, including booleans, subdivision, and any other modifier on the stack. The original object and its modifiers are left untouched. The result is a fresh static mesh with no modifiers.
docs.title: Working with Modifiers

docs.text: Select all the objects you want to crush before clicking Crush . They run at the same time, up to one job per CPU core.
docs.title: Processing Multiple Objects

docs.text: Select the result and click the Revert button next to Crush. It deletes the result and brings back the original. This needs Keep Original to be on. See Keep Original and Revert .
docs.title: Going Back

docs.text: After a Decimate, Last Crush at the bottom of Advanced shows the triangle counts, total time and passes for the active crushed object. Click Details for the time of each phase. After a Remesh, a status box under the Keep section says what the run did (the real quad count and any notes).
docs.title: After Crushing
